name: Vertex AI
oneLiner: Unified platform to build, train and deploy ML and generative-AI models.
whatItIs: Vertex AI is Google Cloud's unified machine-learning platform, bringing training, tuning, deployment, MLOps and generative AI under one roof. You can build custom models (with any framework), use AutoML to train without much code, or call Google's foundation models — including Gemini — through the same platform. It integrates tightly with BigQuery (train on warehouse data, or use BigQuery ML), Cloud Storage and the rest of GCP. Vertex is where GCP data-science teams take models from notebook to production, and increasingly the front door for generative-AI apps on Google Cloud.

inPractice.narrative: A team trains a demand-forecasting model: they pull features from BigQuery, run a custom training job on Vertex (managed compute that scales up then releases), track experiments, and register the best model. They deploy it to a Vertex endpoint the app calls for predictions, and a pipeline retrains it weekly as fresh data lands in BigQuery. For a support-assistant feature, the same platform serves Gemini via the model garden. Managed compute runs only during jobs and while endpoints are live.

coreConcepts.detail: Train your own models (any framework, managed compute incl. GPUs/TPUs) or let AutoML build models for tabular/vision/text with minimal code.
Access Google's foundation models (Gemini) and open/third-party models to tune, deploy or call via API — the generative-AI side.
Deploy models to online endpoints for real-time inference or run batch prediction; managed and autoscaled.
Vertex Pipelines orchestrate repeatable train/eval/deploy steps; the Model Registry versions and governs models; Feature Store serves features consistently.
Train on BigQuery data directly, or push models into BigQuery ML — minimal data movement between warehouse and ML.
Managed Jupyter environments for development, wired into the rest of Vertex and GCP data services.

whenToUse: End-to-end ML on GCP: build, train, tune, deploy, monitor.
Training on BigQuery data with minimal movement.
Low-code model building via AutoML for common tasks.
Building generative-AI apps on Gemini/foundation models.
Productionising models with pipelines, registry and feature store (MLOps).
whenNotToUse: Simple SQL-native predictions on warehouse data — BigQuery ML alone may suffice.
Just calling a hosted AI API with no lifecycle needs — a direct API call is simpler.
Tiny experiments where a local/Colab notebook is enough.

keyFacts.label: GenAI
keyFacts.value: Gemini + foundation models via Model Garden.

pricingShape: Vertex bills for compute per phase: training jobs by the instance-time they use (spun up then released), notebooks while running, and deployed endpoints for as long as they're live — so idle online endpoints, like on any ML platform, bill even without traffic and are the main cost trap. GPU/TPU training is expensive; batch prediction avoids standing endpoints. Foundation-model/Gemini calls are billed by tokens/usage. Storage and BigQuery are separate. Levers: undeploy idle endpoints, right-size training hardware, prefer batch prediction where latency allows.
gotchas: Deployed online endpoints bill while live even with zero traffic — undeploy idle ones or use batch prediction.
Idle Workbench notebooks keep billing — stop them.
GPU/TPU training costs add up fast; match hardware to the job and consider preemptible.
The platform is broad (AutoML, custom, GenAI, MLOps) — easy to over-engineer a simple model.
Generative-model usage is token-billed separately from training/hosting — track it distinctly.
